span.label: The three memory concepts occupy non-overlapping time scales: working memory spans milliseconds to minutes, short-term memory minutes to days, and long-term memory days to years.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Having several distinct storage time scales, rather than one, protects important memories from being erased by the overwriting and interference that ongoing storage would otherwise cause.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Robot experiments in which a fast adaptation process is combined with a slow one produce more complex behaviour than either time scale alone.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Caenorhabditis elegans shows synaptic plasticity but no experience-based structural plasticity, so organisms do not necessarily exploit all available time scales.

The cited name is the subject of a result verb and the sentence carries no first-person marker, so the finding, quantity or definition is the CITED author's rather than this record's. The claim is true and the quote is verbatim - what is wrong is whose result the corpus says it is. Nothing edited, nothing withdrawn: the row is marked so a page can name the source. Where the record is a commentary or review, its `claim_relations` layer usually already names the paper being discussed - the record knows at one layer and forgets at another.

span.label: Of the proposed memory-physiology links, working memory-to-activity and long-term-memory-to-structural-plasticity have experimental support, whereas the classic long-term-memory-to-long-term-plasticity link is still disputed.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Of Martin et al.'s four criteria for tying plasticity to memory, mimicry has never been experimentally realised.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Rats in enriched environments grow significantly more dendritic spines than controls, which the authors read as experimental evidence linking long-term memory to structural plasticity.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Adding synaptic scaling with a quadratic weight dependence to a generic plasticity rule can be shown mathematically to stabilise weight development.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Structural plasticity is modelled only computationally because no analytical models of network topology change exist yet.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Whether the exact human forgetting curve is exponential or a power law remains unsettled.
